screening_decisions.reason: Observational before-and-after study evaluating a primary health care programme, not a randomised controlled trial.
Randomised controlled trial evaluating malaria chemoprophylaxis, not TBA training. The intervention is a drug, not training.
Observational cohort study comparing outcomes based on delivery attendant type and immunisation status, not an RCT.
Field trial evaluating management of childhood pneumonia by various workers including TBAs, not an RCT focused on pregnancy outcomes or TBA training for obstetric care.
Cochrane systematic review of community-based intervention packages, not a primary RCT.
Methodological paper on detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots, irrelevant to TBA training.
Retrospective survey validation study assessing women's self-report of obstetric complications, not an RCT.

Randomised controlled trial comparing lecture-style versus interactive problem-based teaching methods for traditional birth attendants, fitting the criteria for comparing different training approaches.
Quasi-experimental field trial evaluating home-based neonatal care by village health workers; TBA assistance was a component but not the primary randomised intervention.
Controlled study comparing communities with and without access to trained TBAs, but communities were not randomised to intervention (quasi-experimental design).
Review/commentary on a meta-analysis of TBA training effectiveness, not a primary RCT.
Cluster randomised controlled trial evaluating the effect of training traditional birth attendants in neonatal resuscitation and infection management versus standard care on neonatal mortality.
Narrative review summarising perinatal interventions and systematic reviews, not a primary RCT.
Retrospective case record review of postpartum haemorrhage in a teaching hospital, not an RCT.
Pre-post time-series experimental study assessing knowledge and practice of TBAs after formal teaching, lacking a control group and randomisation.

Cluster-randomised controlled trial evaluating an intervention involving training traditional birth attendants and integrating them into the health system versus usual care on perinatal and maternal mortality.
Cluster-randomised controlled trial evaluating women's groups; all clusters received basic TBA training as standard care, so TBA training was not the intervention being compared.
Systematic review analysing causes of maternal death, not a primary RCT.
Quasi-experimental study using a before-and-after design with intervention and non-intervention communities to assess TBA training effects, not an RCT.
Cluster-randomised controlled trial promoting exclusive breastfeeding through health and nutrition workers, not evaluating TBA training.

This is a longitudinal intervention study with intervention and comparison areas, not a randomised controlled trial. While TBAs are involved (>85% of deliveries), the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is a community-based observational study comparing outcomes of infants delivered at TMHs vs hospitals/home. It is not a randomised controlled trial.
This is a review/policy document about the Safe Motherhood Initiative, not a primary research study or RCT.
The abstract describes a study about Episcopal priests and identity work, completely unrelated to TBA training or maternal health. Not an RCT on TBA training.

This is a community randomized trial, but the intervention focuses on nutrition counselling for feeding practices in under-twos. TBAs are mentioned only as one of many counselling channels (32% of caregivers), not as the primary intervention target. Does not compare trained vs untrained TBAs.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques, not a primary study on TBA training. Not an RCT.

This is a cluster-randomized controlled trial that trained birth attendants in Essential Newborn Care and Neonatal Resuscitation Program. The Neonatal Resuscitation Program component was assessed as a cluster-randomized controlled trial comparing trained vs untrained birth attendants across six countries. This meets the selection criteria for RCTs comparing trained versus untrained TBAs.
This is a prospective study examining the accuracy of women's reporting of obstetric complications. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not involve TBA training.

This is a cross-sectional survey of 93 randomly-selected TBAs to understand their knowledge, attitudes, and practices. While it mentions trained vs untrained TBAs, it is not an RCT comparing outcomes.

This study trained TBAs in the intervention area to administer misoprostol for PPH, while non-intervention area TBAs referred women. However, the study design is not described as randomised - it appears to be a quasi-experimental design with intervention and non-intervention areas. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is a review/overview article about global neonatal mortality patterns and causes. It is not a primary research study or RCT.

This is a cluster-randomised effectiveness trial evaluating a community-based intervention package delivered through LHWs working with traditional birth attendants and community health committees. The selection criteria includes 'women cared for/living in areas served by TBAs', and this study involves areas where TBAs are part of the care delivery system. The intervention compares areas with the TBA-involved intervention package vs routine care.
This is a validation study of verbal autopsy methodology for determining cause of death in neonates. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not involve TBA training.
